items_missed: No agenda statement at the open and no timeframe. The call went 'Hi Stein moving this is Dana. Can I have your name?' straight into 'let me check availability for you first.' The closest thing to a roadmap came nine minutes in — 'I'll go ahead and discuss the pricing and then your estimate after' — after the intake was already done, so the customer never knew the call would run 13 minutes.
Never asked 'how are you today?' or any warm-up before jumping to the zip codes.

Origin stories/stairs never asked. She asked 'how many stories does your new have new place have?' for the destination only — the Spring Branch pickup home was never confirmed as single-story, and stairs are the biggest hour driver on a 1300 sqft job.
Special considerations never probed — no question about long walks, narrow hallways, or tight turns at either address, on a rural pickup where walk distance is a real variable.
Storage stops never asked about, and additional stops never asked about. Both came out as assumptions rather than confirmed facts.
Moving stressors never asked. There was no 'is there anything you're particularly worried about with this move?' — and the customer had given an obvious hook with the two mounted TVs.
Meet Your Mover never mentioned — the pre-move email with the mover's photo and info never came up, on a call where the customer specifically praised the human side ('I appreciate your help').

No Worries Damage Coverage delivered but not named, and the dollar figure came through as the wrong number: 'our insurance... provides $52,000 per move to repair, replace or reimburse any accidental damage.' The correct figure is $2,000. The 60¢/lb baseline was never mentioned either, so the customer has no frame for why No Worries matters.

No sense-check after the clock explanation. She ran clock start, 2.5-hour minimum, and 15-minute increments back-to-back and the customer only said 'Okay.' three times — no 'does that make sense?' to confirm the most billing-sensitive part of the call landed.

Truck count never stated in the estimate. She said 'about six and a half to eight and a half hours with two movers' but never confirmed one truck, so the customer has movers without the crew/equipment picture.

Estimate variables incomplete: walk distance never mentioned, no equivalents/school-bus reference used to make the box or time math concrete, and traffic never raised despite her own point that 'the major factor here is the drive time' on a Spring Branch to Liberty Hill haul.

No Save Your Ass prep speech. The only gesture was 'you only pay for the actual time use on the move so it'll all depend on how [prepared] you are' — no consolidation examples (kids' toys, garden tools, loose items in drawers, photos off walls), no 'does that make sense?' close.

Missed the biggest Save Your Ass opening in the call. The customer volunteered 'I'll also be taking some things ahead of time' and 'I think at most probably between five to seven boxes' and Danah answered 'Mm-hmm. Okay. Okay. Alright.' That was a customer already leaning into prep behavior and it got zero reinforcement — no 'take a carload' tip, no explanation that it directly cuts her bill.

No booking attempt. She confirmed 'twenty fourth twenty fifth we have availability' in minute two and then never asked for the business. The customer closed with 'I have probably about three other quotes left for today... I'll be getting back with everybody' and Danah replied 'Sure. Yup.' A live, quoted, available-date lead was let off the phone unbooked with no attempt to hold the 24th.

'No deposit' was customer-prompted, not volunteered — 'what about deposit beforehand' / 'We don't require a deposit.' On a call against three competitors, no deposit is a differentiator that should have been pitched, not answered.

No BOLDED-details framing for the confirmation email and no 'reply with any corrections.' She said 'I'll send everything to your email' three times without ever telling the customer to verify the details — on a job where the box count moved from 45-55 down to 5-10 and the sqft was corrected from 1200 to 1300, verification matters.
Never asked 'any other questions before I let you go?' The customer had to volunteer 'that would complete it on my end.'

Hours and direct contact info never given — just 'if you have any questions Melissa just give us a call,' with no hours and no number, to a customer who explicitly said she was deciding tomorrow morning.
top_strength: The pricing and clock block was the strongest part of this call and close to script-perfect. She opened correctly — 'So pricing very simple' — tiered the rate by day and used it as a selling point: 'Thursday is one of our best value days. So the hourly rate for two movers is $192 now while if you move on Friday, it'll be $206.' That framing worked, because the customer repeated it back at the end unprompted: 'we said the twenty fourth you are paying which was a better rate.' She then covered what's included ('The gas and the truck taxes and insurance... we will wrap all the furniture'), disassembly/reassembly ('we also disassemble and reassemble furniture, and even appliances'), and handled the trip fee like a pro — she gave the number, then immediately justified it: '$335... because both of your location falls outside of our free service zone... that's the flat rate that covers the drive from branch going to your current home then from liberty hill going back to the branch.' The no-hidden-fees pitch followed ('no credit card fees, no special item fees. No this assembly reassembly fees too. So it's only the hourly rate and the trip fee'), then the On-Time Guarantee, then the full clock explanation. Her estimate math was also internally consistent and honest: 6.5-8.5 hours at $192 plus the $335 trip fee lands exactly on the $1,583-$1,967 she quoted, and she flagged the real driver ('your items are very straightforward but the major factor here is the drive time'). She also volunteered unprompted FAQs that build trust — 'anything on the wall we unmount it... but at the new place, we cannot mount it back because of liability reasons' and 'We don't hire daily contracted workers. They're all employed with background checks and professional training.' The customer's closing 'Beautiful, thank you so much. I appreciate your help' was earned.
coaching_note: Highest-leverage fix, by a wide margin: she never asked for the business. Danah confirmed availability in minute two, built a complete and accurate quote, earned real trust, and then handed a comparison-shopping customer the phone back. When Melissa said 'I have probably about three other quotes left for today... I'll be getting back with everybody,' the line Danah needed was: 'Totally fair, Melissa — and here's the thing, there's no deposit and no cancellation fee, so I can lock the 24th in your name right now at the Thursday rate. If someone beats us tomorrow you just call me and I release it, but if you wait and the 24th books up, that better rate goes away. Want me to hold it?' That single ask converts this call. Second priority: the Save Your Ass speech is completely absent, and the customer handed her the opening on a plate — she said 'I'll also be taking some things ahead of time' and Danah said 'Mm-hmm. Okay.' The reply should have been: 'That's actually the single best thing you can do — we bill by the hour, so every carload you take yourself and every drawer you empty ahead of time comes straight off your final bill. Before move day, get the loose stuff consolidated into boxes, pull the photos off the walls, and box up anything small enough to ride in your car. On a 6.5-hour move that can easily save you an hour. Does that make sense?' Given her range topped out at $1,967, that speech is worth real money to this customer and real hours to the crew — and it's the section driving the company-wide gap. Third: fix the coverage number. She told the customer the damage coverage 'provides $52,000 per move' — the real figure is $2,000, and she never named it No Worries or gave the 60¢/lb industry baseline it's supposed to beat. Whether that was her mouth or the transcription needs an audio check, but if she said $52,000 on a recorded line to a customer who is comparing quotes, that's a promise Einstein cannot keep and it needs correcting before the confirmation email goes out. Two smaller closes to build in: ask origin stories/stairs (she only asked the destination), and always end with 'any other questions before I let you go?' plus hours and a direct number — this customer said she was deciding the next morning and left the call without a way to reach Danah specifically.
phone_presence_notes: Genuinely warm and personal — used 'Melissa' seven times, asked permission before the hold ('Can I put you on hold for about three to five minutes, okay?') and thanked her on return, and the customer reciprocated with 'great question' mid-call and 'Beautiful, thank you so much. I appreciate your help' at the end; held back from a 5 by heavy 'Mm-hmm / Okay. Alright. So, yeah' filler and transitions that acknowledged answers without building on them.
audio_review_reason: The damage-coverage figure transcribed as '$52,000 per move' instead of $2,000 — needs an audio listen to confirm whether Danah actually misquoted the coverage to a comparison-shopping customer or whether it is an ASR error. Several other stretches are garbled in ways that affect scoring ('the we o'clock works', 'valuable or refresh items', 'it'll all depend on how, what preferred you are on'), so the Save Your Ass gesture and the clock sense-check cannot be judged from text with full confidence.
